name: Castle Hill and the Old Harbour
tagline: Below the Seljuk walls, with the Red Tower on the quay
description: The headland where the thirteenth century Seljuk fortifications climb the rock, with the Red Tower and the old shipyard on the harbour below and a quarter of Ottoman houses on the slopes. It is the historic heart of Alanya and the quietest part of the central town.
bestFor: Stays that want the castle, the harbour and the old quarter
pros: Seljuk walls and the Red Tower on the doorstep
Views over both bays from the hill
cons: Steep, with a long climb to the upper castle

name: Cleopatra Beach and the Western Strip
tagline: The main beach, with the promenade and the sea-view blocks
description: The long sand beach running west from the headland, backed by a promenade and rows of apartment blocks, many of them owned by the town's large foreign resident population. It is where most arrivals base themselves: swimming from the door, restaurants along the front, everything walkable.
bestFor: Almost anyone arriving, for the beach access and the foreign community
pros: The town's best beach directly there
Restaurants, gyms and services along the promenade
The largest concentration of foreign residents
cons: Highest rents in Alanya, and higher again in summer
Traffic on the coastal road behind

name: Oba and Tosmur
tagline: East of the centre, newer complexes and better value
description: The residential districts east of the river, where much of Alanya's newer apartment building has gone up in complexes with pools and gardens, aimed at both Turkish families and foreign buyers. It is quieter than the strip, cheaper for a better flat, and ten minutes from the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a modern flat with a pool at a moderate rent
pros: Newer, better-built apartments with shared pools
Quieter, with a year-round resident population
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes to the main beach
Car or dolmus needed for most things

name: Mahmutlar
tagline: The high-rise suburb east, where the foreign residents concentrate
description: A dense strip of apartment towers about twelve kilometres east, built almost entirely for foreign buyers over the last two decades, with supermarkets, its own market day and a large permanent Russian, Ukrainian and northern European population. Rents are the lowest for a sea view anywhere here.
bestFor: Long stays wanting a cheap sea-view flat and an established foreign community
pros: The cheapest sea-view apartments in the area
cons: Dense high-rise development with little charm

name: Dim Cayi and the Taurus Foothills
tagline: Up the river valley, cool water and pine forest
description: The valley of the Dim river inland from the town, where riverside restaurants sit on platforms over cold running water and the road climbs into the Taurus pine forest towards the Dim cave. It is noticeably cooler than the coast and a genuine escape from the summer heat.
bestFor: Stays that want the river and the mountains rather than the beach
pros: Cool river water and forest at the door
Considerably cooler than the coast in summer
cons: Twenty minutes to the beach and the town
Very few services and slower internet
